question: On the full frozen ironflow_bulk panel (18 monthly parquet, 2025-05..2026-10), does the Shek (2026) funding-extreme correction pattern reconstruct: is the median/mean time for an extreme funding observation to correct back to its pre-extreme band LONGER in a high realized-volatility regime than in a low regime, and is the correction hazard LOWER when realized volatility is higher, clearing a frozen materiality floor with Holm-adjusted uncertainty?

design.event_definition: funding extreme: |funding_rate| >= q_t where q_t is an EXPANDING, TRAIN-ONLY quantile of |funding_rate| per coin (no future information)
design.correction_definition: first subsequent hour the funding rate returns inside the pre-extreme band (|funding_rate| < q_t) within a frozen maximum horizon; censored events recorded as censored, never as completed negatives
design.regime_split: realized-volatility tercile (high vs low) from trailing 24h close-to-close log returns, train-only thresholds

walk_forward.note: chronological expanding train-only thresholds; no overlapping forward targets across the purge boundary

estimands: correction hazard (survival) contrast high-RV vs low-RV
inference: Holm step-down over the declared family
design.materiality_rule: the high-vs-low RV regime contrast in median correction time must exceed >= 10% relative in the slower-correction direction
design.verdict_rule: symmetric: PROMOTED if materiality_met and direction slower; else NOT_SUPPORTED; INCONCLUSIVE if a regime median is undefined

bootstrap.method: percentile bootstrap of the median correction time

paper_claim.source: Shek (2026) 'Limits to Coordination: Funding Drag in Crypto Perpetual Funding Rates' (SSRN 7529458)
paper_claim.claim: lower correction hazard with higher realized volatility
paper_claim.treatment: working-paper claim to reconstruct, not established truth

do_not: re-run the broad RV-forecast (FCLR-VOL-BROAD-01, closed NOT_SUPPORTED)
build a risk overlay (forecast gate not passed)
threshold-shop or relax the frozen floor after outcomes
